newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN OPEN WITH WIN OVER ITALY.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDEN OPEN WITH WIN OVER ITALY.

text.p: Jorgen Jonsson scored twice to lead Olympic champions Sweden to a 5-3 win over Italy in their opening game at the world championship on Saturday.
Clinging to a 4-3 lead, Jonsson scored the third period's only goal to clinch the victory and keep Sweden's 100 per cent record against Italy in 11 world championship events intact.
Sweden appeared to take control of the contest midway through the second period when Michael Nylander and Niklas Sundblad scored s 64 seconds apart to make it 4-2.
But Gaetano Orlando knocked in a loose puck from a goalmouth scramble to notch his second of the period and cut the deficit to one.
Orlando scored his first of the game when he slipped a rebound into an open net, pulling Italy even at 2-2.
The goal came just 40 seconds after defenceman Marcus Ragnarsson of the San Jose Sharks had begun the period by giving Sweden a 2-1 lead.
The two teams had traded goals in the opening period, Jonsson putting Sweden on the scoreboard first and Mario Chittaroni replying for Italy.
New York Islanders netminder Tommy Salo was solid in the Swedish goal, particularly during the third period.
